thread:
sam_sales: FYI Globex POC load test -> getting 429s around 10-15s into the run. Demo tomorrow 11am PT, can we triage?
ben_infra: on it. which route are they hitting and token sizes?
sam_sales: /v1/generate-chat primarily, some embeddings calls mixed in. They run parallel workers, ~8 conc, average prompt ~1.2k tokens, responses ~600-1k.
mina_sre: ok that feels like burst + per-route cap. Can you drop a sample request id or logs?
devon_support: customer pasted this error snippet: `{"error":"rate_limited","code":429,"message":"route_quota_exceeded: per-route burst window"}`
ben_infra: thanks. Checking ratecap metrics now. Looks like their tenant has a per-route burst window of 30r/s and a sustained route cap of 10r/s. Their parallel workers are spiking instantaneous RPS above that.
sam_sales: they said they only requested a small trial bump; wanted to keep engineering changes minimal. Any quick mitigation we can suggest before the demo?
mina_sre: two quick options: (1) ask them to lower client concurrency to 3-4 for demo, or (2) temporary per-route burst increase for the tenant for next 24h. Also enable token-based accounting insight so we can confirm token budget isn't being exhausted.
devon_support: i can propose (1) to them. If they want (2) we'll need approval. @ben_infra can you confirm no upstream capacity issues?
ben_infra: infra is healthy. No global throttles. This is strictly tenant-level per-route enforcement. I can flip a temporary bump on the auth side: increase burst window to 100r/s and route cap to 20r/s for 12h. Need sign-off from sales ops.
sam_sales: i'll get ops sign-off. In parallel, can we surface a short explanation for the customer so they understand what's happening?
mina_sre: send them this blurb they can paste into their infra notes: "Redwood enforces per-tenant, per-route burst windows to protect shared capacity. Your current config allows short bursts up to X requests/second but sustained throughput is capped. For POC demos we can temporarily increase your burst window or recommend lowering parallel client workers. Long-term we recommend using batching/prefix KV caching to lower per-token cost and RPS."
devon_support: logging snippet from their tenant (redacted):
```
[2026-03-20T18:22:14Z] tenant=globex route=/v1/generate-chat request_id=req_0a1b2c status=429 reason=route_quota_exceeded current_window=12 burst_limit=30 sustained_limit=10 tokens_in_window=18420
```
ben_infra: tokens_in_window looks high — token accounting counts both prompt+response. With avg 1800 tokens/request * 8 conc ~= 14.4k tokens in a single second-ish; that aligns.
mina_sre: also check client retry behavior. If their SDK retries aggressively on 429 without backoff it can amplify bursts. Ask them to implement exponential backoff and jitter.
sam_sales: good call. i'll tell them to dial concurrency down + enable backoff. Ops approved temporary bump for demo. ben_infra can you apply 12h bump now?
ben_infra: applying now. runbook command: `POST /internal/admin/tenants/globex/limits {"route":"/v1/generate-chat","burst":100,"sustained":20,"expires_in":"12h"}` — done. deploy-bot: limit-change: tenant=globex route=/v1/generate-chat burst=100 sustained=20 expires=2026-03-21T06:45:00Z (UTC)
deploy-bot: ✅ change applied, config propagation to edge nodes in ~30s.
devon_support: told customer: "We temporarily increased your per-route burst for 12h and recommend lowering client concurrency + adding exponential backoff. We'll monitor and revert after demo." They replied :thumbsup:.
mina_sre: monitoring — watching occupant metrics. If we still see sustained high token usage we should consider enabling prefix caching or advising a quantized model for POC.
ben_infra: added a dashboard panel under tenant/Globex -> per-route RPS, token-window, 429-rate. I'll share link in DM.
sam_sales: perfect. thanks team — close loop after demo.
mina_sre: one follow-up for internal notes: root cause = mismatch between client concurrency + large avg token lengths -> tenant per-route burst window exceeded; not a global outage. Remediation = temporary per-route bump + client tuning + retries/backoff.
notes: Contains root + replies; short Slack-style messages, logs, config snippets, bot confirmation.
